title: Infective Endocarditis: Recognition, Blood Cultures and Urgent Referral

evidenceAudit.scope: Recognition, microbiological sampling, imaging and endocarditis-team escalation for suspected infective endocarditis.
findings: Rebuilt against the approved-topic structure: a tiered investigation panel, time-ordered management and an explicit medicine decision pathway.
Every investigation row includes a reference or normal state, condition finding and next action.
Previous outline and published rows remain preserved; this additive version is pending clinical review.
unverifiedSections: No topic-specific Saudi national guideline was found in the opened Saudi Ministry of Health protocol index unless a Saudi source is explicitly cited in the medicine row.
Current live Saudi Food and Drug Authority product registration was not individually confirmed; clinicians must check the hospital formulary.
Local antibiogram, resistance pattern, shared-care agreement and imaging availability require site-level confirmation where relevant.

pathophysiology.summary: Bloodstream organisms adhere to susceptible endocardial or prosthetic surfaces. Vegetation can destroy valves and cause heart failure or abscess. Emboli and immune phenomena can injure brain, spleen, kidney and other organs.
keyMechanisms: Bloodstream organisms adhere to susceptible endocardial or prosthetic surfaces.
Vegetation can destroy valves and cause heart failure or abscess.
Emboli and immune phenomena can injure brain, spleen, kidney and other organs.

references.title: 2023 ESC Guidelines for the management of endocarditis

symptoms: Fever, rigors, fatigue, breathlessness, weight loss, focal pain or neurological symptoms.
physicalSigns: New or changing murmur, heart failure, embolic signs, vascular/immunological lesions or persistent bacteraemia.
redFlags: Pulmonary oedema, shock, conduction block, focal neurology, persistent sepsis, prosthetic-valve/device infection or large embolic burden.
precipitants: Prosthetic valve, previous endocarditis, cardiac device, structural heart disease, haemodialysis, injection drug use or recent bacteraemia.

differentials.distinguishingFeatures: No endocardial imaging finding or persistent clinical pattern; organism and host risk still matter.
Sterile vegetation in malignancy/autoimmune disease with negative microbiology.
Systemic inflammatory features without a microbiological or endocardial source.

diagnosticCriteria.threshold: Apply the current ESC-modified diagnostic criteria using microbiology, imaging and clinical features; do not use one negative study to exclude high-probability disease.

ruleIn.testName: Three sets of peripheral blood cultures
ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Obtain before antibiotics when stable enough; document separate venepunctures and timing.

ruleIn.testName: Full blood count and inflammatory markers
ruleIn.normalValue: White-cell count 4.0–11.0 ×10⁹/L; inflammatory markers below local upper limits
ruleIn.expectedFinding: Anaemia, leucocytosis and raised inflammatory markers
ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Supports systemic inflammation and provides a treatment baseline.

ruleIn.normalValue: Creatinine within local range; no blood or protein in urine
ruleIn.expectedFinding: Acute kidney injury, haematuria or proteinuria
ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Detects immune or embolic renal injury and guides antimicrobial dosing.

ruleIn.normalValue: Sinus rhythm without new conduction delay
ruleIn.expectedFinding: New atrioventricular block or other conduction change
ruleIn.clinicalRationale: A new conduction abnormality can indicate peri-annular extension and needs urgent escalation.

ruleIn.normalValue: No vegetation, abscess or new valvular dysfunction
ruleIn.expectedFinding: Vegetation, new regurgitation, abscess or prosthetic complication
ruleIn.clinicalRationale: First-line cardiac imaging; a negative study does not exclude high-probability disease.

ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Use when suspicion remains high, prosthetic/device infection is possible or transthoracic imaging is inadequate.

ruleOut.normalValue: No pathological periprosthetic or extracardiac uptake
ruleOut.expectedFinding: Abnormal uptake supporting prosthetic infection or metastatic focus
ruleOut.clinicalRationale: Use within the endocarditis-team imaging pathway, especially for prosthetic material.

ruleOut.testName: Brain and body imaging for complications
ruleOut.normalValue: No embolus, infarct, haemorrhage or abscess
ruleOut.expectedFinding: Embolic infarct, haemorrhage, mycotic aneurysm or metastatic infection
ruleOut.clinicalRationale: Image urgently for focal symptoms and before decisions affected by neurological complications.

clinicalManagement.title: Stabilise and obtain cultures
actions: Treat shock or heart failure and obtain three blood-culture sets before antibiotics when this is safe.
If unstable, take cultures promptly and start the local empirical endocarditis regimen without avoidable delay.

clinicalManagement.title: Image valves and complications
actions: Arrange transthoracic echocardiography followed by transoesophageal imaging when indicated.
Use brain/body imaging for focal or embolic complications through the specialist pathway.

clinicalManagement.title: Activate the endocarditis team
actions: Discuss with cardiology, infectious diseases/microbiology and cardiac surgery.
Escalate heart failure, uncontrolled infection, abscess/conduction block and embolic-risk features for early surgical assessment.

medicationPlan.note: Obtain three blood-culture sets before antibiotics when the patient is stable enough. Empirical therapy depends on native/prosthetic valve, acquisition setting, prior antibiotics and local resistance and must follow the endocarditis team. The regimens shown are selected organism-directed pathways from ESC Tables 7–10. Current live SFDA registration was not individually confirmed; check the hospital formulary.

regimens.patientGroup: Adult with susceptible oral-streptococcal or Streptococcus gallolyticus native-valve endocarditis
regimens.duration: 4 weeks for native-valve endocarditis; 6 weeks for prosthetic-valve endocarditis
adjustments: Confirm organism and susceptibility with microbiology.
Review hepatic and renal function when both are severely impaired.
Ceftriaxone is listed in the Saudi Essential Medicines List; current live SFDA registration was not individually confirmed.
monitoring: Blood cultures until clearance, temperature and inflammatory response.
Full blood count, renal/liver profile and echocardiographic complications.
contraindications: Do not use this branch for resistant isolates or an unconfirmed organism.

regimens.patientGroup: Adult with methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus native-valve endocarditis
regimens.frequency: Divide into 2–3 doses and individualise by therapeutic drug monitoring
adjustments: Use pharmacy-led therapeutic drug monitoring and renal adjustment.
Account for obesity, unstable renal function and renal replacement therapy.
Vancomycin is listed in the Saudi Essential Medicines List; current live SFDA registration was not individually confirmed.
monitoring: Blood cultures until clearance and serum vancomycin exposure using the local protocol.
Renal function and urine output at least daily during instability.
contraindications: Use enhanced caution with acute kidney injury or concurrent nephrotoxins.

regimens.indication: Cell-wall active component of definitive dual beta-lactam treatment
adjustments: Adjust for renal impairment with pharmacy/microbiology advice.

monitoring: Blood cultures until clearance, renal/liver profile and full blood count.
contraindications: Do not use without the paired ceftriaxone in this branch.

teaching.scope: Recognition, microbiological sampling, imaging and endocarditis-team escalation for suspected infective endocarditis.
learningObjectives: Recognise the condition and its red flags.
Choose initial tests without delaying urgent escalation.
Use a named multidisciplinary disposition plan.
keyPoints: Pulmonary oedema, shock, conduction block, focal neurology, persistent sepsis, prosthetic-valve/device infection or large embolic burden.
Discuss with cardiology, infectious diseases/microbiology and cardiac surgery.
pitfalls: Stopping after a short outline instead of documenting the full investigation pathway.
Using a medicine row without checking the branch, allergy, organ function, culture result and local formulary.
Mistaking publication status for clinical approval; this version remains pending until a clinician approves it.

patientEducation: Explain the working diagnosis, immediate plan and specific return or deterioration signs.
lifestyleAndDiet: Address prevention and self-management only after the acute safety plan is complete.
dischargeCriteria: Not suitable for routine discharge before endocarditis-team assessment; outpatient treatment requires a formal specialist plan and stability criteria.
nonClinicalManagement.followUpPlan: The endocarditis team defines antimicrobial duration, repeat cultures/imaging, surgery, oral health and relapse surveillance.
